newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Jan-June direct investment up 53 pct-report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Jan-June direct investment up 53 pct-report.

text.p: Foreign direct investment in Brazil totaled $7.3 billion in the first six months of 1997, up almost 53 percent from the same period last year, Gazeta Mercantil said.
The newspaper, citing a source at the Central Bank, said foreign direct investment slipped to $1.0 billion in June from $1.7 billion in May.
It said the May result was unusually high because of the selloff of a majority stake in state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce for over $3.0 billion.
The source told Gazeta that direct foreign investment was financing about half of the country's current account deficit, which is expected to top 4.0 percent of gross domestic product this year.
Foreign direct investment should reach about $15 billion this year, with auto investment contributing a good share. Brazil drew $9.0 billion in foreign investment in 1996.
